title: Rommel's counterattack broken
photoNote: "North American B-25 and other unidentified planes on a mission over Western Desert, Egypt." U.S. Air Force photo 23326 A.C. (filed under Bombing; mount stamped received 28 Dec 1942 from the Western Desert, released 24 Dec 1942, credit Yank, the Army newspaper). NARA 342-FH, naId 204943770, unrestricted, public domain. A falling bomb and a stick of bombs are visible below the formation. Exact mission date not recorded; American B-25s of the 12th Bombardment Group flew with the Desert Air Force during El Alamein. Cropped from the mounted print.
body:
Rommel gathered his panzers for one more blow at El Alamein. The bombers found them first.

28 October 1942. Rommel's 15th and 21st Panzer Divisions attacked the British line near Kidney Ridge and were stopped by gun and tank fire. That afternoon they massed to try again. Allied aircraft bombed them as they formed up, and the second attack never got going.

Rommel never seized the initiative at El Alamein again. Within a week, his army was in retreat.

alt: Archival 1942 photo taken from a bomber: an American B-25 over the Western Desert with a formation of bombers and fighters ahead, a stick of bombs falling toward the ground and one more bomb dropping below. Text: 28 OCT 1942, El Alamein, Egypt. Broken before it began.

video.note: Desert Victory (1943), British Ministry of Information documentary with film shot by the Army Film and Photographic Unit and RAF cameramen; Crown copyright expired, public domain (PD-UKGov on Wikimedia Commons; 480p copy from Brian's Source Film folder). From the film's air attack sequence, which its narrator introduces with the enemy armor moving north and 'the air force began the task of preventing them from concentrating'. Clip uses 41:14.45 to 41:16.10 (bombers in formation, bomb released), 41:18.95 to 41:20.95 (bombs falling over the desert), 41:10.40 to 41:12.60 (guns firing up), 41:16.18 to 41:17.93 (gun firing), 41:21.02 to 41:22.60 (bomber releasing), and 41:33.00 to 41:39.30 (cockpit, then bombs bursting below). Sound: the film's own soundtrack under these shots (bombs, guns, engine drone). The film's score plays under the formation shots at 40:41 to 41:05 and in a short run at 41:23 to 41:31, so those are left out; checked by spectrogram, and no narration by speech recognition. Normalized to -16 LUFS.
video.hook: The bombers found the panzers first.

kit.filmCaption: Film of Allied bombers over El Alamein, October 1942, with the film's own sound: bombs released over the desert, guns firing up at them, and the bursts below. On 28 October, air attacks broke up Rommel's panzers as they gathered to counterattack. From the 1943 British documentary Desert Victory.
